$comment: W47 G0 (c): W46's label grammar (results/2026-10-05-w46-g0-declaration/fit/labels.json), ported by
copy, with a short name and a scale for every X67 key (charter X67; Decision Log 5): operator 1's
tintAlphaFar1x / 2x (t1, t2; 1x, 2x), the occlusion gain (o; both), the span tops (m1, m2; 1x, 2x), the
receded body width optics.regular.blurSigma (b; both: a device-px width read at every scale) and operator
2's share and widths (u, both; v1, v2; 1x, 2x). The grammar's invariants hold: no short name begins with
the receded mark and none is a prefix of another (test_fit.py reads every slot and leaf back). W46's
comment follows.
W46 G0: the ONE label grammar of W46's candidates, read by build-candidate.ts (the pattern a label must
match) and by search.py (how a point is named). The tracker's W45 entry: search.py marked a receded leaf
with an upper-case R, which the builder's [a-z0-9.-] refused, so stage 2 could not build its first point.
Here the marks and the pattern are stated once, both are lower-case, and test_fit.py builds a label of
every slot and leaf through the real builder. No short name begins with the receded mark and none is a prefix of another, so a
label part reads back to one (slot, leaf).
`scales`: the scale each leaf acts at (`rampAtScale` anchors every 1x/2x pair and the 2x-only leaves),
read by fit.py's scale-separable rendering: a point renders each scale through its scale twin, the
candidate of its overrides restricted to the leaves acting there. A leaf with no entry refuses. Exact
only under the anchoring, which the ladders verify (every lever rendered at both scales, the scale it
does not act at byte-identical to the control's).
`gates`: a tap's share and what it gates (W47 G0, the review of stage 1's crossed factorial). At share 0 no
second (or fine) texture exists, so the tap's widths and W45's far share are unread (the identity table's
gate-group for the widths; W45's far share 'unread at share 0', proved by render in w45-share-far.spec.ts):
search.py holds them at their start there, so a crossed factorial does not offer a tap-off point twice. And
a tap whose width resolves to 0 at a scale draws nothing at that scale (W30's rule: the pyramid builds no
texture at width 0 and the shader does not enter the mix), so fit.py's scale twin drops the share at that
scale and the unread leaves at a scale where the share resolves 0. Ladder (ii) verifies the first by
requiring every 1x capture byte-identical to the snapshot rung's.
